Joseph Prifitera — Founder & CEO, OPSAVOR

The POS should be the system of record—not the owner’s operating brain.
That lesson is why I’m building OPSAVOR.
After operating in restaurants, I saw how often sales, labor, schedules, vendor invoices, and expenses live in different places. The owner becomes the integration layer: hunting for numbers, reconciling reports, and figuring out what changed after the fact.
OPSAVOR is being built to give owners a clear operating picture: what changed, what needs attention, and what action to take next. Restaurants are our starting point because the problem is real, expensive, and deeply familiar.
We’re early, building through a controlled pilot at Sicily Coal Fired Pizza and learning directly from operators. The goal is simple: help independent owners spend less time chasing information and more time running a stronger business.
If you’re a restaurant owner, operator, or building in restaurant technology, I’d love to compare notes.
